item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it adds the requested buffered Upload API without altering global retry or Files.Add behavior. Both patches incorrectly duplicate Add instead of routing through it, and both have incomplete tests, but A additionally makes expressly out-of-scope behavioral changes to RawClient.","reasons":["B preserves FilesService.Add behavior and confines production changes to the files service.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile, validates inputs, and propagates multipart/source-reader errors.","A changes retry, Content-Length, and reader-ownership semantics for every seekable RawClient body, contrary to the contract's scope restrictions and requirement to preserve Add behavior.","A's GetBody implementation reuses one mutable io.ReadSeeker rather than producing independent bodies, which is a fragile global mechanism and may be unsafe if GetBody consumers overlap or invoke it unexpectedly."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of the required existing Add method, duplicating option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.","The broad RawClient modification affects Files.Update, Persons.AddPicture, and unrelated callers despite the contract forbidding retry refactoring.","wireSeekableRequestBody can leave the reader at EOF if seeking back to the original position fails after successfully seeking to the end."],"risks_b":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of delegating to Add, violating a specific contract requirement and creating duplicate machinery.","The retry test supplies bytes.NewReader, so it does not demonstrate that an originally non-replayable streamed content reader is buffered and retried.","There is no test using a reader that returns an error, although the implementation appears to propagate multipartbody.NewFile errors."]}
